_authored: tools-free, authored by the Wave B mission 2026-09-09 from the MBTA V3 API, extended by Wave B2B with the feasibility arithmetic and by Wave B2C with the MBTA's own design criteria and the station as built. Not generated; edit deliberately.
what: Green Line E infrastructure adjacent to Northeastern, as FACTS plus the arithmetic that decides what can be built from them. Track, catenary AND the two side platforms are now runtime geometry (src/world/Transit.js) on a local station section of Huntington (src/data/boston-geo.js).
attribution: MBTA V3 API - https://api-v3.mbta.com (MBTA open data)

MBTA GLX Design Criteria Manual, Revision 2, January 2014 - https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/2018-11/2014-11-12-glx-design-criteria-manual-rev2.pdf (MBTA engineering standard, published openly). Read as REFERENCE for numeric criteria; no text or drawing is reproduced in this repository.

platformArrangement.note: GTFS gives one stop point per direction. They are BOARDING ANCHORS - no extents, no width, no platform_code; the 'platformName' values are direction labels ('Heath Street', 'Park Street & North'), not platform identifiers.

measuredAgainstGameCorridor.method: projected onto edges 486/487/488 sampled at 300 stations each; perp = signed offset from the corridor centreline
measuredAgainstGameCorridor.whyThisSettlesIt: The two directional points sit on OPPOSITE sides of the corridor 7.77 m apart, while two track centres are 3.40 m apart. Read as track centres they would put one track at +4.32 m - outside the 3.50 m reservation, in the eastbound traffic lane. Read as platform centroids they would put a platform in the same place. They are boarding anchors and nothing else.
measuredAgainstGameCorridor.caveat: These perpendicular values also inherit the 5.9 m road-position error in routeShape, so they are not evidence about where the REAL platforms are either. Both readings say the same thing: do not use these points as geometry.

realWorld.source: MassGIS/MassDOT Roads via docs/neu/SOURCES.md - public domain, already vetted by this project
realWorld.medianNote: the median widens to 48 ft across the campus and IS the Green Line E reservation

asBuiltInGame.edge: Huntington Avenue, arterial; lanesDeclared 4 in src/data/boston-geo.js, resolved to lanes 2 (one per direction) by RoadNetwork.laneLayout once the median is declared
asBuiltInGame.medianM: 7.00 outside the station section, 11.20 inside it
asBuiltInGame.note: Wave B2A gave the road a central reserved median. halfRoad stays 9.80 m and the parking bay stays at 8.55 m, so the footway, the graded W_VERGE crossing and the starter-SUV parking solution are all untouched; what changed is that the four lanes at -5.25/-1.75/+1.75/+5.25 became one lane per direction at -5.25/+5.25 and the middle 7.00 m is reserved. The game centreline is the CORRIDOR CENTRE - the average of the two directional carriageways - which is also the real reservation centre, so the reservation is in the right place even though its width is authored.

waveCPrerequisite: Settle the contact wire height deliberately: either bring it to the GLX 15'-0" above top of rail, or record the street-running reason for keeping it higher as a decision rather than a deviation.
A moving trolley, if it is ever wanted, now has track, wire and two platforms to serve.
Lettering on the name blade needs a sign-atlas tile and a second material; decide whether one draw call is worth a legible station name.
halfRoad and the kerb line stay fixed at 9.80 m. The footway, the graded W_VERGE crossing and the parking lane outside the station must not move.

fiveDistinctQuantities.why: Wave B2A's notes were shortened to 'two tracks at ~1.5 m gauge', which collapses five different measurements into one and makes the station look feasible when it is not. They are kept apart here.

1_railGaugeM.means: rail head to rail head WITHIN ONE TRACK. The MBTA Green Line is standard gauge.
1_railGaugeM.note: This is the number people quote as '1.435' or loosely '~1.5'. It says nothing about how far apart two tracks are.

2_trackCentreToCentreM.means: centreline of track 1 to centreline of track 2.
2_trackCentreToCentreM.note: Cannot be derived from MBTA data: the published route shape is a single polyline shared by both directions - see routeShape. 3.40 m is ordinary for street-running light rail and is what src/world/Transit.js lays. Outer rail lands at 2.4175 m from the reservation centre.
2_trackCentreToCentreM.derivation: 1.70 (half of 3.40) + 0.7175 (half gauge) = 2.4175 m; reservation half-width is 3.50 m, so 1.0825 m clear.

3_platformSetbackFromNearestRailM.means: how far the platform edge must stand off, so a car body clears it.
3_platformSetbackFromNearestRailM.note: Green Line low-floor cars are about 2.85 m over the body, so half-envelope 1.425 m from track centre. Measured from the RAIL rather than the track centre it is 1.425 - 0.7175 = 0.7075 m, which is why quoting a setback without saying what it is measured from is useless.

4_platformWidthM.means: usable width of the platform itself.
4_platformWidthM.note: 2.00 m is about the least that carries a shelter, a wheelchair turn and a waiting queue. 0.375 m is what the 7.00 m reservation actually leaves: 3.50 - 1.70 - 1.425.

5_reservationWidthM.confidence: asBuilt C - authored; realWorld A - MassGIS
5_reservationWidthM.means: kerb-to-kerb width of the central reserved band.
5_reservationWidthM.note: The real 14.6 m median cannot be spent in this model: the game's Huntington is ONE corridor centreline with halfRoad frozen at 9.80 m, and 14.6 m of median inside +/-9.80 m leaves 2.5 m per side for everything else. 7.00 m is the largest reservation that still leaves a travelled lane and the kerbside parking bay - see src/data/boston-geo.js for the same reasoning at the source.

routeShape.offsetMethod: median of perpendicular distance over 1.2 km of corridor; every sample the same sign
routeShape.conclusion: UNUSABLE as track geometry, for two independent reasons: one polyline cannot yield two track centres, and the offset from this project's Huntington is larger than the whole 3.40 m spacing being placed. The offset is the known road-position error recorded in docs/neu/GAPS.json, not a discovery about the median.

twoTracks.arithmetic: outer rail at 1.70 + 0.7175 = 2.4175 m; reservation half-width 3.50 m; clear 1.0825 m
twoTracks.mastClearance: centre mast is 0.22 m square, so its face is 0.11 m from the reservation centre and 1.59 m from a track centre, against a 1.425 m vehicle half-envelope: 0.165 m clear. Tight, and the reason centre-pole reservations are spaced the way they are.

twoTracksPlusTwoSidePlatforms.arithmetic: 3.40 (track centres) + 2 x 1.425 (vehicle half-envelope) + 2 x 2.00 (platform) = 10.25 m needed against 7.00 m available; deficit 3.25 m
twoTracksPlusTwoSidePlatforms.whyNotJustBuildItNarrow: 0.375 m is not a platform. It is narrower than a person. Building it to avoid reporting the gap would put a decorative sliver where a boarding platform belongs.

wideningInsideTheFrozenKerb.verdict: GEOMETRICALLY POSSIBLE, needs a capability the road model does not have
wideningInsideTheFrozenKerb.arithmetic: a 10.25 m reservation has half-width 5.125 m; from there to the kerb at 9.80 m is 4.675 m, against 3.50 m of lane plus 0.30 m of shoulder = 3.80 m needed. 0.875 m clear - IF kerbside parking is suspended, which is exactly what real stops do.
wideningInsideTheFrozenKerb.blockedBy: B2A's median is declared PER EDGE. The frontage edge 486 is 389.5 m long and carries the parking bay the starter SUV resolves against, so widening it would suspend parking over 389 m to serve a 60 m stop. Sub-edge granularity is the missing capability.

blockerResolvedByWaveB2A.was: A factual Green Line reservation cannot be built without first making Huntington a divided road, and that moves every locked artefact of the canonical opening.
blockerResolvedByWaveB2A.resolution: Wave B2A added the reserved-median section to Roads.js/RoadNetwork.js with lane layout, parking and the kerb line all derived AROUND the band rather than across it. halfRoad 9.80 and parking 8.55 are unchanged, 530 other edges are untouched, and traffic on the median edges drives at +/-5.25 with nothing inside the reservation.
keptForTheRecord: There is no median or reservation concept anywhere in the road system: no field, no band, no section support.
halfRoad is DERIVED from lane count: halfRoad = (lanes/2)*laneW + shoulder + park. Dropping Huntington from 4 lanes to 2 to free ~7 m of median takes halfRoad from 9.80 m to 6.30 m.
That moves the kerb line inward 3.5 m, and with it the footway, the graded W_VERGE crossing accepted in 35d56ae, and the parking lane whose offset (8.55 m) the starter SUV solver resolves against.
Holding halfRoad by overriding street width sets `lw`, which disables lane markings entirely (`marks = ... && !lw`) and replaces real lane centres with a naive division.
So a median needs NEW section capability in Roads.js - a reserved band that lane layout, parking and the kerb line all respect.

blockerRemaining.summary: CLOSED by Wave B2C. Both platforms are built.
blockerRemaining.wasNeeded: sub-edge reservation width: a median that can widen over a stop's length with kerbside parking suspended only there, instead of one width per 389 m edge.
blockerRemaining.howItWasClosed: A street may now declare `sections` - world-space spans that override the reserved width and the kerbside bay along part of an edge, with their own taper. Measured against origin/main with no section declared, all 540 edges are bit-identical in cross-section, edge polyline and lane path geometry; with the station declared, exactly one edge differs.

builtInWaveB2B.collidersNote: 0 by design and measured: a car driven onto the reservation crosses all four rail heads with four wheels down, flat ride height and no damage, and a character walks across them with no snag. Rails that collided would be a trap in the middle of an arterial.

visibilityFromTheCanonicalOpening.method: 366 rail-centreline samples along edges 486/487/488, tested against the cold-boot camera frustum (eye -1883/4.775/1677, bearing 65 deg, fov 55) and then raycast for occlusion against every other mesh in the scene
visibilityFromTheCanonicalOpening.verdict: MARGINAL. 12 of 366 samples - 3.3% - survive occlusion, at 18.9 m and beyond, at the right-hand edge of the frame; they are not legible in the frame at 1x. The nearest reservation point is at bearing 228 deg, i.e. BEHIND the player: the opening looks into the Krentzman quadrangle, not at Huntington.
visibilityFromTheCanonicalOpening.correction: The commit message on d545165 says the railway 'is what the player sees from the opening'. That overstates it. The railway is what the player sees on the canonical WALK from the quadrangle to the starter SUV, which ends on the Huntington footway with the reservation across the street. The first frame is the quadrangle.

designCriteria.source: MBTA GLX Design Criteria Manual, Rev 2, January 2014
designCriteria.whyThisSource: It is the MBTA's own criteria for Green Line light rail, published openly on mbta.com. Before Wave B2C the track spacing, the platform setback and the platform height were all confidence-C authored numbers; three of them are now the MBTA's, and one authored value turned out to be within 23 mm of theirs.
designCriteria.caveat: These are the criteria for the Green Line EXTENSION, i.e. new build on an exclusive alignment. Northeastern is an existing street-running stop. The CLEARANCE criteria carry over because they are about the vehicle; the 225 ft platform length does not, and is not used as one - see platformExtents.

trackGauge.value: 4' 8-1/2" measured 5/8" below top of rail, on the gauge face

trackCentresMainline.qualifier: the table is stated 'without center catenary poles'
trackCentresMainline.verdict: 3.40 m is above the absolute minimum and below the preferred one. It is unchanged from B2B and was not re-derived: Wave B2C was told not to redesign the accepted rail system without a real conflict, and there is none - see centrePoles.
trackCentresMainline.confidence: criteria A; the 3.40 m as-built remains C - authored

centrePoles.criterion: the criteria call for side poles and say that 'where this arrangement is not possible due to property restriction, center poles located between tracks shall be used'
centrePoles.verdict: A 7.00 m reservation inside a 19.60 m carriageway IS a property restriction, so the centre-pole arrangement this project already built is the criteria's own fallback rather than a shortcut.

platformEdgeToTrackCentre.value: 4'-9" for platforms located on tangent track
platformEdgeToTrackCentre.note: This replaced an authored 1.425 m, which came from half a 2.85 m car body. The two agree to 23 mm, which is why the authored cross-section survived contact with the standard.

platformHeightAboveTopOfRail.value: 8 inches at the edge, with 14 inches recorded as the future state 'to accommodate level boarding into the Type 9 LRVs'
platformHeightAboveTopOfRail.whyEightAndNotFourteen: The MBTA's own facility data for place-nuniv lists a PORTABLE_BOARDING_LIFT for each direction - 'Customers can board/exit certain trains using mobile lift'. A stop that boards wheelchairs with a mobile lift is a stop without level boarding, so 8 inches is the honest height here and NO accessible boarding claim is made for it.

platformGap.value: no larger than 3 inches, conforming to ADA
platformGap.note: Recorded for completeness. Not modelled: there is no vehicle.

platformLength.value: 225 feet, 'in order to accommodate a single three-car LRV'
platformLength.derived: 225 ft / 3 cars = 75 ft = 22.86 m per car, which is the only vehicle length in this file and is derived from the MBTA's own figure rather than from a fleet page - mbta.com does not publish car dimensions.
platformLength.notUsedDirectly: 225 ft is a GLX new-build island platform. Northeastern is a street stop with mobile lifts; claiming a 69 m accessible island here would be a fabrication.
platformLength.confidence: A for the criterion, not applicable as an extent here

clearanceEnvelopeMethod.formula: CE = VDE + OWF + RC, referenced from the centreline of track at top of rail
clearanceEnvelopeMethod.note: The numeric vehicle dynamic envelope lives in a referenced drawing (BSP Dwg. No. 1018) that is not published with the manual, so the envelope half-width used elsewhere in this project stays authored.

knownDeviation.criterion: 15'-0" above top of rail on the right of way; 16'-0" in yards 'because of truck traffic beneath the wires'
knownDeviation.asBuilt: 5.60 m above the reservation surface, i.e. about 5.46 m above top of rail = 17'-11"
knownDeviation.verdict: DEVIATION, ACCEPTED AND RECORDED. Wave B2C was scoped not to redesign the accepted catenary without a real clearance conflict, and a wire that is too HIGH is not one. The criteria's own reasoning for raising it in yards - road vehicles underneath - applies to a street reservation. Left for Wave C to settle deliberately rather than changed in passing.
knownDeviation.confidence: criterion A; the deviation is a project decision

platformExtents.label: PROJECT-AUTHORED PLATFORM EXTENTS, ANCHORED TO MBTA DIRECTIONAL BOARDING POINTS
platformExtents.noSurveyClaim: No extent for this stop exists in the open data. Three queries confirm it: /stops returns platform_code null for both directions; /facilities returns only the two mobile lifts, with no dimension property; and the two other stop ids the lift records exclude (41391, 81317) are BUS stops on Huntington, not further rail boarding points.
platformExtents.lengthDerivation: two thirds of the MBTA's own 225 ft three-car platform criterion, i.e. two cars
platformExtents.anchorPlacement: the boarding point is taken as three quarters along its platform in the direction of travel, on the reasoning that a train stops with its front at the far end. This is an ASSUMPTION; the data does not say where on a platform its boarding point sits. It is also what leaves room for the outbound taper to finish before the junction 41 m beyond it.
platformExtents.staggerSource: the measured along-corridor separation of the two boarding points, preserved as-is
platformExtents.sideAssignment: from the SIGNS of the projected boarding points - outbound +4.32 m, inbound -3.45 m - which is what right-hand running requires. The magnitudes are unusable and the caveat below still stands.

stationSectionAsBuilt.whyShyOffset: At exactly 10.30 m of reservation - the width the platform arithmetic alone asks for - the platform's back face lands on the travelled lane's own edge with nothing between them, and that face is a raised 0.34 m kerb 46 m long, twice. 11.20 m buys the offset and still leaves 0.40 m at the kerb.

cost.roadTrianglesDelta: +3864, from densifying edge 486's polyline 22 -> 63 points and the finer ribbon sampling that a taper needs

remainingGaps: No vehicle. A trolley remains deliberately deferred, and nothing here needs one.

The name blade carries NO lettering. Legible text needs a new tile in the sign atlas, which would put the platform on a second material and cost a draw call for a 1.9 m panel. The station reads by form and route colour instead.
The contact wire sits about 0.9 m higher than the GLX criterion - see designCriteria.knownDeviation.

`city.roads.parkingAllowedNear(x, z)` resolves through `nearestEdge`, so within a metre or two of a node it can bind to the neighbouring edge and answer for that one instead. Measured effect at this station: none - the parked-car audit finds 0 cars in the suspended span - but the by-edge and by-world forms are known to disagree at s=384 of edge 486, where the taper has already returned the median to 7.004 m.

docs/neu/TRANSIT.json still reports `railStations: 0`, `railAlignments: 0`, `surfaceTrolley: false`. It is generated by tools/neu-audit/build.mjs and is not hand-edited; its OSM-derived way counts are also ODbL, so regenerating it is a separate decision.
